title: 第一章 考城隍第十章孝子第十一章促织
lines: 第一章考城隍
宋焘觉得自己大概是死了。
这个念头来得并不突然。他已经病了小半个月，起初只是风寒，后来越来越重，请了几位郎中都摇头。母亲每日守在床前，煎药喂药，眼看着他一天比一天瘦下去。他心里着急，却连说话的力气都没有。
这天午后，他迷迷糊糊地伏在书案上，忽然觉得身子一轻，像是有什么东西从躯壳里抽了出来。他低头一看，自己还趴在桌上，笔掉在地上，墨汁洇了一摊。
他伸出手去捡笔，手却穿过了笔杆。
果然死了。他想。
奇怪的是，他心里并不怎么害怕。只是有些遗憾——母亲还在，他若死了，谁来奉养？
正在这时，一匹白马从虚空中走出来，通体雪白，没有一丝杂色。马上坐着一个公差，穿着古旧的官服，脸看不清楚，像隔着一层水雾。
“宋焘，跟我走。”公差的声音很平，没有催促，也没有安慰，像是在说一件再寻常不过的事。
“去哪？”
“考试。”
宋焘还想问，人已经被拉上了马。白马腾空而起，向着一片光亮奔去。风从耳边呼啸而过，他下意识闭上眼睛，再睁开时，已经到了一座宫殿前。
台阶是白色的，汉白玉的质地，却比任何汉白玉都要温润，像是用月光砌成的。台阶向上延伸，看不到尽头，越往上越亮，到最后几乎融进了光里。
公差递给他一块牌子，上面写着一个字：“孝”。
“进去吧。考完了就知道了。”
宋焘握紧牌子，开始往上走。
他走了十几步，忽然发现台阶两侧有东西。不是雕刻，也不是画，而是像水面倒影一样的画面，随着他的步伐一帧一帧地浮现。
第一幅画面里，母亲坐在油灯下缝衣服，他在旁边读书。母亲的眼睛不好，凑得很近，针脚却还是歪歪斜斜的。她叹了口气，把那片衣料拆了重新缝。
第二幅画面里，母亲端着一碗药走进来。他的脸烧得通红，母亲把药吹凉了，一勺一勺喂他。喂完之后，她用手背试了试他的额头，又试了试自己的，眉头皱得很深。
第三幅画面里，母亲跪在佛像前。她没有哭，只是一遍一遍地磕头，额头磕在地上，发出沉闷的声响。佛前的香灰落下来，落在她的白发上。
宋焘的脚步慢了下来。
第四幅画面里，母亲坐在门槛上，望着村口的路。她的背佝偻了，手不停地搓着一块布，搓了又展开，展开了又搓。那是他小时候的一件衣服，早就不能穿了，她却一直留着。
第五幅画面里，母亲躺在床上。不是睡着的姿势，是病着的姿势。她脸色蜡黄，嘴唇干裂，却还是撑着想坐起来。邻居大婶按着她，说你别动了，焘儿去给你抓药了，一会儿就回来。她点点头，眼睛却一直望着门口。
宋焘站住了。
他站在台阶中间，上也不是，下也不是。那些画面还在继续，一帧一帧地往后翻，像是有人故意让他看的。他知道后面是什么——母亲病重那三个月，他日夜守在床前，端汤喂药，擦身换衣，没有一夜合过眼。母亲临终前拉着他的手，已经没有力气说话了，嘴唇动了动，他知道她说的是“焘儿，你要好好活着”。
宋焘闭上眼睛，深吸一口气，继续往上走。
到了最后一阶，那些画面都消失了。面前是一座大殿，殿门开着，里面空荡荡的，只有两张桌子。一张桌子前已经坐了一个人，三十来岁，面色苍白，穿着洗得发白的青衫，正襟危坐，面前摆着一张试卷。
宋焘走过去，在另一张桌前坐下。桌上也有一张试卷，上面只有一个题目：
“一人二人，有心无心。”
他看着这八个字，一时不知道从哪里下笔。
content_en:
Chapter 1 Examination of the City God
Song Tao felt that he was probably dead.
This idea did not come suddenly. He had been ill for less than half a month. At first it was just a cold, but then it became more and more serious. Several doctors who invited him shook their heads. His mother stayed at his bedside every day, cooking and feeding him medicine, watching him lose weight day by day. He was anxious, but he didn't even have the strength to speak.
That afternoon, while he was lying on his desk in a daze, he suddenly felt a lightness in his body, as if something was being pulled out of his body. He looked down and saw that he was still lying on the table, his pen fell to the ground, and the ink smeared.
He reached out to pick up the pen, but his hand passed through the pen barrel.
Sure enough, he died. he thought.
The strange thing is that he doesn't feel much fear in his heart. It's just a little regretful - his mother is still here, if he dies, who will take care of him?
At this moment, a white horse walked out of the void, completely white without a trace of color. Immediately, an official sat down, wearing an old official uniform. His face could not be seen clearly, as if he was separated by a layer of mist.
"Song Tao, come with me." The official's voice was calm, without urging or comforting, as if he was saying something ordinary.
"Where to go?"
"Exam."
Song Tao still wanted to ask, but the man had already been pulled onto the horse. The white horse soared into the sky and ran towards the light. The wind whistled past his ears, and he subconsciously closed his eyes. When he opened them again, he was already in front of a palace.
The steps are white, and the texture of the white marble is gentler than any other white marble, as if they were built with moonlight. The steps extend upwards with no end in sight, getting brighter and brighter as they go up, until they almost merge into the light.
The official handed him a sign with one word written on it: "filial piety".
"Go in. You'll know after the exam."
Song Tao held the sign tightly and started walking up.
He walked a dozen steps and suddenly noticed something on both sides of the steps. It's not a sculpture or a painting, but a picture like a reflection on the water surface, emerging frame by frame as he steps.
In the first picture, his mother is sitting under an oil lamp sewing clothes, and he is reading next to her. My mother's eyesight is not good, so even though she was very close, the stitches were still crooked. She sighed and took apart the piece of fabric and sewed it again.
In the second scene, the mother walks in with a bowl of medicine. His face was burning red, and his mother blew the medicine to cool it down and fed him spoonful by spoonful. After feeding, she tried his forehead with the back of her hand, and then her own, frowning deeply.
In the third picture, the mother is kneeling in front of the Buddha statue. She did not cry, but kowtowed over and over again, hitting her forehead on the ground with a dull sound. The ashes from the incense in front of the Buddha fell down and landed on her white hair.
Song Tao's pace slowed down.
In the fourth picture, the mother is sitting on the threshold, looking at the road at the entrance of the village. Her back was stooped, and her hands kept rubbing a piece of cloth, rubbing it and unfolding it, unfolding it and rubbing it again. It was a piece of clothing from his childhood. He could no longer wear it, but she kept it.
In the fifth picture, the mother is lying on the bed. It's not a sleeping posture, it's a sick posture. Her face was sallow and her lips were chapped, but she still tried to sit up. The neighbor's aunt held her down and said, "Don't move." Tao'er went to get some medicine for you and would be back soon. She nodded, but kept looking at the door.
Song Tao stopped.
He stood in the middle of the steps, neither up nor down. Those pictures were still going on, flipping back frame by frame, as if someone had deliberately let him see them. He knew what was coming next - during the three months when his mother was seriously ill, he stayed by the bed day and night, serving soup and medicine, wiping himself and changing clothes, and never slept a night. Before his mother died, she held his hand. She no longer had the strength to speak, and her lips moved. He knew that what she said was "Tao'er, you have to live well."
Song Tao closed his eyes, took a deep breath, and continued walking up.
At the last level, those images disappeared. There was a large hall in front of him. The door of the hall was open and it was empty except for two tables. There was already a person sitting in front of a table. He was about thirty years old, with a pale complexion, and was wearing a washed green shirt. He was sitting upright, with a test paper in front of him.
Song Tao walked over and sat down at another table. There is also a test paper on the table, with only one question on it:
"One person and two people, intentional or not."
He looked at these eight words and didn't know where to start.
